campbell.title: Campbell City Council — August 18, 2026
campbell.summary: The Campbell City Council considered routine business including approving past meeting minutes and city bill payments, along with new labor agreements for police officers and carpenters union employees. The Council also reviewed a police foundation donation, a bond oversight committee report, and administrative items like conference delegate selection and a city clerk contract update.
keyTopics: New two-year labor agreements (2026-2028) with the Campbell Peace Officers Association and North Coast States Carpenters Union
Acceptance of $41,911.62 in Campbell Police Foundation donations for K9 veterinary care, equipment, and support
FY 2025 Annual Report from the Citizen's Bond Oversight Committee for Measure O
Designation of voting delegates for the 2026 League of California Cities Annual Conference
Merit increase amendment to the City Clerk services agreement

saratoga.title: Saratoga City Council — June 3, 2026
saratoga.summary: The Saratoga City Council considered options for the level of law enforcement service it contracts for with the Sheriff's Office for the coming fiscal year. Council members were asked to choose among the service level options the Sheriff proposed and give staff further direction based on that choice.
keyTopics: Selecting a Sheriff's Office service level option for FY 2026
Providing staff direction following the Council's near-term Sheriff service approach

los-gatos.title: Los Gatos Town Council — August 18, 2026
los-gatos.summary: The Los Gatos Town Council considered a routine set of administrative and financial items, including monthly financial reports, accounts payable and payroll approvals, and a professional services agreement. The Council also took up an omnibus ordinance updating the Town Code, a second amendment to an existing agreement, and a request regarding whether to continue or hear a public hearing on appeals.
keyTopics: Monthly Financial and Investment Report for June 2026
Agreement for professional services authorized for the Town Manager to execute
Omnibus ordinance amending the Town Code with minor updates
Second amendment to an existing agreement
Request to continue or hear public hearing appeals

san-jose.title: San José City Council — August 26, 2026
san-jose.summary: This was a procedural Rules and Open Government Committee meeting focused on setting the agenda for the upcoming September 1, 2026 City Council meeting. The committee also reviewed the public record from mid-August, considered an appointment to the VEBA Advisory Committee, and noted a joint special meeting with the San José/Santa Clara Treatment Plant Advisory Committee.
keyTopics: Setting the final agenda for the September 1, 2026 City Council meeting
Review of the public record for August 13-20, 2026
VEBA Advisory Committee appointment
Joint special meeting with the San José/Santa Clara Treatment Plant Advisory Committee
Cancellation of the September 8, 2026 draft agenda review

mountain-view.title: Mountain View City Council — August 25, 2026
mountain-view.summary: The Mountain View City Council met in closed session to discuss personnel matters involving two of its own appointees, the City Clerk and City Manager. The meeting also included a performance evaluation of these unrepresented employees and a discussion with labor negotiators regarding their terms, plus time for public comment on items not otherwise on the agenda.
keyTopics: Performance evaluation of the City Clerk and City Manager (Council appointees)
Closed-session labor negotiation discussion involving the City Clerk and City Manager as unrepresented employees, with Vice Mayor Clark as the city's designated negotiator
Public comment period for topics not listed elsewhere on the agenda

sunnyvale.title: Sunnyvale City Council — August 25, 2026
sunnyvale.summary: The Sunnyvale City Council held a closed session followed by a special meeting focused on a presentation. The public portion of the meeting centered on an update to the CleanWater Program.
keyTopics: Closed session (non-public discussion)
CleanWater Program update presentation

cupertino.title: Cupertino Teen Commission — August 12, 2026
cupertino.summary: The Cupertino Teen Commission met to discuss an upcoming Bike Fest, a Juvenile Traffic Diversion Program, and a youth-led organization called Next Vision AI. The Commission also considered approval of minutes from its June 10, 2026 meeting.
keyTopics: Bike Fest planning
Juvenile Traffic Diversion Program
Next Vision AI, a youth-led organization
Approval of June 10, 2026 meeting minutes

santa-clara.title: Santa Clara City Council — August 25, 2026
santa-clara.summary: This Santa Clara City Council meeting was held in a hybrid format, with in-person attendance and remote participation options via Zoom or phone. One Councilmember (Chahal) joined remotely from India. The provided agenda excerpt did not include substantive policy items beyond meeting logistics and public comment procedures.
keyTopics: Hybrid meeting format with in-person and remote (Zoom/phone) participation options
Councilmember Chahal participating remotely from Panchkula, India

milpitas.title: Milpitas City Council — August 11, 2026
milpitas.summary: The Milpitas City Council considered introducing an ordinance amending part of the city's municipal code, and received an educational presentation on municipal bonds basics. The meeting also included routine business such as approving past meeting minutes and reviewing upcoming agenda items.
keyTopics: Introduction of an ordinance amending Municipal Code Title XIII, Chapter B.6
Presentation on Municipal Bonds 101 basics for the council
Review of the City Council meeting calendar
Approval of prior City Council meeting minutes
Preview of items expected at the next regular City Council meeting

palo-alto.title: Palo Alto Public Art Commission — August 20, 2026
palo-alto.summary: The Palo Alto Public Art Commission reviewed final plans for a public art installation at 3150 El Camino Real, with a presentation from the project's art consultant, artist, and developer team. Commissioners also considered funding for a temporary interactive media art program and the acceptance of donated artworks from two local artists for the city's collection.
keyTopics: Approval of June 18, 2026 meeting minutes
Final review and approval of public art plan for the 3150 El Camino Real private development, with presentation by artist Giles Miller, consultant Danielle Wohl, and Acclaim Companies
Allocation of up to $70,000 for temporary Code:ART 2027 interactive media installations
Acceptance of donated artworks by CASP artists Adrienne Defendi and Eric Fei into the city's public art collection
